summary.oneLiner: Goodyear India Limited is the Indian tyre arm of The Goodyear Tire & Rubber Company group, manufacturing farm and commercial truck bias tyres at its Ballabgarh plant and marketing Goodyear passenger car tyres, tubes and flaps in the Indian replacement market.
summary.business: The Company manufactures and sells automotive tyres, namely farm tyres and commercial truck bias tyres, at its Ballabgarh plant. It also markets and sells passenger car tyres manufactured by Goodyear South Asia Tyres Private Limited ('GSATPL'), Aurangabad, in the replacement market, along with tubes and flaps. It serves both the Farm OE channel (tractor manufacturers) and the Farm and Consumer replacement channels, with the farm tyre business positioned as its leadership franchise.

risks.risk: Portfolio concentration in Farm with limited Commercial (Truck & Bus) presence
risks.note: The Indian tyre industry is dominated by the Commercial category, which contributes more than 50% of industry revenue; the Company's limited presence there restricts portfolio selling and its ability to mitigate the risk of the Farm category.
Natural rubber and crude oil derivatives constitute a significant portion of tyre production costs, and fluctuations in these prices can severely impact profitability.

risks.risk: Dependence on the agricultural cycle and monsoon
risks.note: Erratic monsoon patterns, fluctuating reservoir levels, adverse weather and heatwaves can hit agricultural output and rural incomes, directly affecting farm tyre demand in both OE and replacement channels.

risks.risk: Parent-level strategic review of the India farm tire business
risks.note: The ultimate parent, The Goodyear Tire & Rubber Company, announced in April 2025 an intention to review all strategic, operational and financial options for the farm tire business; the review concluded on December 5, 2025 with a decision to retain ownership, but the announcement itself caused headwinds and the Farm OE segment declined -7% year-on-year.

risks.risk: Intense competition and product portfolio gaps
risks.note: The Farm Replacement segment declined on account of portfolio gap and intense competition, and the Company competes aggressively for share while relying on new launches and channel expansion to close white spaces.

Slower than expected growth, sticky core inflation, fiscal constraints, geopolitical tension, shifts in US trade policy, reciprocal tariffs and volatile commodity prices (especially oil) are external risks flagged by management.

risks.risk: Climate change adaptation and physical/supply-chain resilience
risks.note: Management recognises that climate change poses the risk of moderate to severe physical events affecting operations and/or the supply chain, and chronic weather conditions could affect raw material supply; business continuity plans, climate risk modelling and GPSNR participation are the stated mitigants.

Uncertainty and complexity from current and emerging regulations will likely require the Company to keep evolving its manufacturing operations, use of materials and/or business model, with non-compliance capable of impacting operations and the ability to conduct business.

risks.risk: Supply chain transparency and sustainable sourcing
risks.note: Identifying, evaluating and addressing environmental and societal impacts across suppliers is flagged as a material risk, managed through the Goodyear Supplier Code of Conduct covering child labour, working conditions, safety, business ethics, environmental practices and anti-corruption.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Goodyear India Limited is the Indian tyre arm of The Goodyear Tire & Rubber Company group, manufacturing farm and commercial truck bias tyres at its Ballabgarh plant and marketing Goodyear passenger car tyres, tubes and flaps in the Indian replacement market.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company manufactures and sells automotive tyres, namely farm tyres and commercial truck bias tyres, at its Ballabgarh plant. It also markets and sells passenger car tyres manufactured by Goodyear South Asia Tyres Private Limited ('GSATPL'), Aurangabad, in the replacement market, along with tubes and flaps. It serves both the Farm OE channel (tractor manufacturers) and the Farm and Consumer replacement channels, with the farm tyre business positioned as its leadership franchise.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body: - The Goodyear Tire & Rubber Company — related party: Group parent whose Innovation centers in Akron, USA and development centre in Kunshan assist the Company's new product development and R&D; the Company's systems and procedures are based on the Goodyear global Quality Management System, and R&D results are not used by other Goodyear affiliates

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Farm:** Farm tyres (tractor tyres)
- **Commercial:** Commercial truck bias tyres
- **Consumer / Passenger:** Passenger car tyres (manufactured by GSATPL, marketed in the replacement market), Assurance Maxguard SUV
- **Other:** Tubes, Flaps

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Farm OE (tractor original equipment manufacturers)
- Farm replacement market in India
- Consumer / passenger car replacement market in India
- Commercial truck (bias) tyres
- Export market for tractor farm tyres

certifications.title: Certs (RHP)
certifications.body:
- ISO 9001 - Quality Management System (recertified in 2024)
- ISO 14001 - Environmental Management System (recertified in 2023)
- Systems and procedures based on the Goodyear global Quality Management System

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Rapid 'SUV-fication' of the market: consumer preference for SUVs and crossovers is shifting demand toward larger 16-inch to 19-inch and above tyres, which command higher price points and better margins
- Emergence of the EV segment, with the industry adapting through EV-ready tyres offering low rolling resistance to maximise battery range
- Premiumization - urban consumers increasingly willing to pay for technologically superior products rather than just mileage
- Digital integration in the purchase journey, forcing manufacturers to strengthen their digital connect with end users
- Sustainability and circular economy push toward 'Green Tyres' using sustainable silica, recycled rubber and bio-based oils
- Farm demand supported by stable replacement demand, increasing farm mechanization and continued growth in the tractor population; mid-to-long-term (3-5 year) growth momentum expected from structural demand and rising rural prosperity
- FY 2026-27 outlook positive on expectations of a normal monsoon, strong rabi crop prospects, higher wheat output and continued government support via higher MSP and multiple DBT schemes
- Trend toward larger rim specifications projected to catalyse significant volume growth in the Consumer Replacement segment
- Structural weakness: the Indian tyre industry is dominated by the Commercial (Truck & Bus) category contributing more than 50% of industry revenue, while the Company has limited presence there, restricting portfolio selling and its ability to mitigate Farm-category risk
- Headwinds flagged: raw material price volatility in natural rubber and crude oil derivatives, erratic monsoon patterns, fluctuating reservoir levels, persistent inflationary pressures, geopolitical uncertainty and intense competition
- Macro backdrop: resilient domestic consumption supported by rising disposable incomes and urbanization, offset by geopolitical tension, energy price volatility and India's reliance on imported crude oil

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Work toward Goodyear's vision of becoming #1 in Tires and Service in India by delivering best-in-class products for evolving customer needs
- Strategically prioritise the premium Luxury, SUV and EV replacement segments and larger rim sizes to drive margin expansion and profitability
- Modernise the product portfolio through new launches - Assurance MaxGuard SUV for the mid-SUV segment and Ultra Grip tractor tyre for varied Indian soil and field conditions
- Expand the distribution footprint and deepen national presence by strengthening channel partnerships, improving product availability and enhancing retail and service touchpoints
- In Farm OE, strengthen customer service and deepen key account relationships; in Farm Replacement, pursue channel expansion, channel engagement and operational excellence so the right tyre is available at the right place, right time and optimal cost
- Apply technology and analytics to boost customer engagement and productivity, and strengthen the digital connect with end users
- Preserve and strengthen leadership in the Farm business through efficient, competitive and customer-centric operations
- Community engagement through structured CSR programmes aligned to Goodyear's Better Future mission and its Safe, Smart and Sustainable focus areas (Hunar Se Udaan skilling, road and tyre safety awareness, Cleaner Air Better Life and Greenbelt)
- Distributions are made through an annual final dividend recommended by the Board in line with the Company's Dividend Distribution Policy and declared by members at the AGM - for Financial Year 2025-26 a final dividend of Rs. 26.50 per fully paid-up equity share of Rs. 10 each has been placed before the 65th AGM for declaration. Managerial remuneration in excess of the Section 197 limits paid for FY 2025-26 is being regularised by seeking members' approval, through special resolutions, for waiver of its recovery from the Managing Director and from all Directors / Executive Directors.
- Goodyear is committed to achieving net-zero greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions across its value chain by no later than 2050
- Near-term science-based targets by 2030: reduce Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions by 46 percent and target Scope 3 GHG emissions by 28 percent, compared to a 2019 baseline
- Decarbonization targets validated by the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi) in September 2023, aligned with limiting global temperature rise to no more than 1.5 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels
- Decarbonization strategies focused on GHG-intensive parts of the business - purchased goods & services, energy and transport - plus additional targets to reduce rolling resistance and tyre weight to improve use-phase emissions
- Circularity commitment covering resource use, operational waste and end-of-life tyres (ELT), using circular materials where possible to reduce depletion of natural resources
- Business continuity plans, climate-event modelling and insurance-informed investment decisions to build climate resilience across locations; participation in the Global Platform for Sustainable Natural Rubber (GPSNR) to mitigate supply chain risk
- Suppliers required to comply with Goodyear's Supplier Code of Conduct (or a comparable code) covering child labour and working conditions, safety, business ethics, environmental practices, anti-corruption, competition law compliance, conflicts of interest and privacy
- Advanced mobility identified as an ESG-linked opportunity as transport transitions to low- or zero-emission solutions, opening new products, services and better tyre life-cycle management
- Grievance redressal through a vigil mechanism policy available to employees, value chain partners and investors, plus Goodyear's confidential Integrity Hotline available 24 hours a day worldwide
- Awards and recognition for supply chain governance (India's Tyre Supply Chain Champions, ISCM) and workplace culture (Best Organizations to Work For 2025, ET Edge)

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The routed sections disclose no new plant, line or capacity-expansion project with a commissioning or ramp timeline. Manufacturing remains concentrated at the Ballabgarh plant (farm tyres and commercial truck bias tyres), while passenger car tyres sold in the replacement market are manufactured by Goodyear South Asia Tyres Private Limited ('GSATPL'), Aurangabad. The principal expansion thrust is commercial rather than physical: after The Goodyear Tire & Rubber Company communicated in April 2025 its intention to undertake a strategic review of the Company's farm tire business and then confirmed on December 5, 2025 that it had concluded the review and decided to retain ownership, the Company stated it remains committed to the continued strengthening and expansion of its farm tire business in India. Alongside this, the Company is expanding its distribution footprint and deepening national presence through stronger channel partnerships, improved product availability and enhanced retail and service touchpoints, and is modernising its portfolio with launches such as the Assurance MaxGuard SUV for the mid-SUV segment and the Ultra Grip tractor tyre.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Sustained leadership position in the Indian Farm tyre business through efficient, competitive and customer-centric operations
- Access to The Goodyear Tire & Rubber Company's innovation centre at Akron, USA and development centre at Kunshan for new product development and R&D support
- In-house farm tyre testing facility enabling new product industrialization and launches with minimum lead time, and product benchmarking
- Brand leverage and equity of the Goodyear brand in the Indian replacement market
- Distribution and channel reach being deepened through channel expansion and tech-enabled service enhancements
- Plant Optimization (PO) / GPS methodology driving plant reliability, productivity and process waste reduction
- Recognized among India's Tyre Supply Chain Champions by the Institute of Supply Chain Management (ISCM) for supply chain governance, planning discipline and operational efficiency
- Recognized as one of the Best Organizations to Work For 2025 by ET Edge

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Portfolio concentration in Farm with limited Commercial (Truck & Bus) presence — The Indian tyre industry is dominated by the Commercial category, which contributes more than 50% of industry revenue; the Company's limited presence there restricts portfolio selling and its ability to mitigate the risk of the Farm category.
- Raw material price volatility — Natural rubber and crude oil derivatives constitute a significant portion of tyre production costs, and fluctuations in these prices can severely impact profitability.
- Dependence on the agricultural cycle and monsoon — Erratic monsoon patterns, fluctuating reservoir levels, adverse weather and heatwaves can hit agricultural output and rural incomes, directly affecting farm tyre demand in both OE and replacement channels.
- Parent-level strategic review of the India farm tire business — The ultimate parent, The Goodyear Tire & Rubber Company, announced in April 2025 an intention to review all strategic, operational and financial options for the farm tire business; the review concluded on December 5, 2025 with a decision to retain ownership, but the announcement itself caused headwinds and the Farm OE segment declined -7% year-on-year.
- Intense competition and product portfolio gaps — The Farm Replacement segment declined on account of portfolio gap and intense competition, and the Company competes aggressively for share while relying on new launches and channel expansion to close white spaces.
- Macro and geopolitical uncertainty — Slower than expected growth, sticky core inflation, fiscal constraints, geopolitical tension, shifts in US trade policy, reciprocal tariffs and volatile commodity prices (especially oil) are external risks flagged by management.
- Climate change adaptation and physical/supply-chain resilience — Management recognises that climate change poses the risk of moderate to severe physical events affecting operations and/or the supply chain, and chronic weather conditions could affect raw material supply; business continuity plans, climate risk modelling and GPSNR participation are the stated mitigants.
- Regulatory compliance and decarbonization transition — Uncertainty and complexity from current and emerging regulations will likely require the Company to keep evolving its manufacturing operations, use of materials and/or business model, with non-compliance capable of impacting operations and the ability to conduct business.
- Supply chain transparency and sustainable sourcing — Identifying, evaluating and addressing environmental and societal impacts across suppliers is flagged as a material risk, managed through the Goodyear Supplier Code of Conduct covering child labour, working conditions, safety, business ethics, environmental practices and anti-corruption.
